title: NU extends UAAP cheerdance reign with 3-peat; UE cops historic silver
summary: The untouchable NU Pep Squad rules the UAAP Cheerdance Competition anew for a title three-peat and record-extending 10th championship, while UE wins its first silver medal in 24 years

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The kings and queens of UAAP cheerdance still sit comfortably on their well-earned thrones.

For a record-extending 10th time in UAAP history, the NU Pep Squad is the UAAP Cheerdance Competition champion, adding another title three-peat to its dynastic history on Saturday, November 21 at the packed Mall of Asia Arena.

With its latest golden coup for double-digit titles, the Gab Bajacan-coached squad created a two-championship gap from the league’s long-tied second-placers, the legendary eight-time titlists UST Salinggawi Dance Troupe and UP Pep Squad.

Taking its act from Japan last year to Mexico on Saturday afternoon, NU embodied a tribal, ritualistic spirit, and took the capacity 21,126-strong crowd on an Aztec whirlwind, highlighted by a literal whirlwind toss to kickstart one of its multiple perfect pyramids.

Meanwhile, the UE Pep Squad — perennial middle-of-the-pack performers — finally broke a nine-year podium drought with a unique Chinese martial arts routine, embodying a true Red Warrior spirit for its first silver finish in 24 long years, or since Season 65 in 2002.
Completing the top three, the FEU Cheering Squad extended its podium run to eight straight seasons with its third consecutive bronze medal after a deliberately paced Aladdin routine.
The Adamson Pep Squad, who wowed the crowd with its extreme motorsports-themed routine, barely missed the mark as it snapped a two-year podium run that produced back-to-back silver medals.
